article.title: DSA NPC Gives Raman Last Chance on Endorsement - YDSA
article.content: The Democratic Socialists of America’s National Political Committee (NPC) passed two resolutions on October 26, each one giving Los Angeles mayoral candidate Nithya Raman an opportunity to clarify her position on Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions(BDS) The resolution rescinding Raman’s endorsement passed, amended, 14-13. It calls for a meeting to be held on October 31. During the gathering Raman will be asked the following questions: Do you support the Palestinian call for Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) to pressure Israel until it complies with international law by ending the occupation, instituting equal rights for its Palestinian citizens and respecting Palestinian refugees’ right to return? What is your stance on pressuring the Israeli government to end its occupation of Palestine? Have you publicly called for a permanent ceasefire in Gaza? Do you commit to refrain from any and all affiliation with the Israeli government or Zionist lobby groups, including rejecting any future endorsements by Democrats for Israel LA? Do you pledge to oppose legislation that harms Palestinians, including the IHRA definition of anti-semitism and buffer zones protecting illegal land sales, and support legislation that supports Palestinian liberation? If Raman fails to attend, or answers these questions insufficiently, the NPC will invalidate DSA-LA’s endorsement on November 1, and will instruct DSA-LA to halt the use of chapter resources to support Raman’s campaign. The second resolution on expelling Raman also passed, amended, 15-12 . It requires Raman meet with DSA-Los Angeles leaders by November 30 to affirm her support for BDS, and sign onto a petition calling for halting weapons shipments to Israel from LAX. If she fails to meet with DSA-Los Angeles leadership, or fails to commit to these demands, a process will begin to expel her from DSA by January 1, 2027. Lasting nearly two hours, the October 26 meeting was filled with heated debate not only about Raman, but what DSA’s relationship to its electeds should be. “We should support socialist candidates, and we should support the best candidates who are not just the best option in race, and the most progressive candidate in race, but the ones actually willing to advance socialist candidates,” said NPC member Francesca Maria. She is also a member of Springs of Revolution Caucus, who opposed DSA LA’s endorsement and lobbied for rescidinding it . Some NPC members had harsh words for DSA-Los Angeles. “This is a crisis of the creation of the DSA-LA Steering Committee,” said Ahmed Husain, who argued that supporting Raman was “trading the lives of one group of people for minor improvements of the lives of people here.” During the meeting, DSA-Los Angeles member Clayton Ryles read an emailed statement from Nithya Raman, an original copy of which was obtained by The Activist . “I believe the best way for working Angelenos to stand in solidarity with Gaza is through non-violent protest, legislative action, and diplomatic pressure, including BDS,” read the email. “As mayor, I will continue to protect the rights of all people to engage in peaceful protests and would continue to oppose any policy or city legislation imposing penalties on the constitutional right to protest against or criticize any nation.” “She has moved closer to our position consistently through our campaign,” argued NPC Member Jeremy Cohan, adding that punishments, if enacted, would have little impact since “this is the eve of a general election.” Others were unimpressed. “I just don’t know how the statement that she supports people’s right to engage in BDS now in 2026 is different from her statement in 2020 saying she supports people’s right engage to engage in BDS, but she herself doesn’t support it,” commented NPC member Andrew Thompson. While critiquing Raman’s inconsistency, Abdullah Farooq-NPC leader and member of DSA- Los Angeles- said reprimanding his chapter and Raman would damage DSA long term. “I think that in this moment, what we need to focus on number one is building a strong organization that’s strong nationally,” Farooq said. “ So building up our chapters across the country, but in particular building up LA, which is a critical node in the supply chain for Israel.” Farooq argued that “pushing towards an intervention that restricts chapters from using their own funds to canvass for a candidate or support a candidate is bringing us any closer to that stronger organization.” “We as the NPC, have to show to our members, who are not members of DSA-LA, that we are willing to articulate a political vision,” said NPC member Sid Carlson White. “There are tens of thousands of members across the country, whose work this endorsement makes significantly harder.” Despite both resolutions passing, the value of this outcome was unclear to some members of the NPC. “I’m struggling to see what goals this accomplishes as written,” said Frances Gil. “I don’t see how it does anything to move DSA-LA members and align around a clear vision of what our electoral work should mean.” The October 26th meeting was the culmination of a monthslong conflict between DSA’s national leadership, DSA-LA, and Nithya Raman, who is running against incumbent Karen Bass to be mayor of Los Angeles. This conflict centers around “ For a Fighting Anti-Zionist DSA ,” a resolution that passed at DSA convention in August of 2025. It sets expectations for how DSA endorsed elected officials and candidates should support Palestine and Palestinian liberation. Support for the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) movement, opposition to legislation that harms Palestinians, and refusing to affiliate with the Israeli government or “Zionist lobby groups,” like AIPAC or the Democratic Majority for For Israel are all listed as requirements for a candidate to get DSA support. One month after the resolution’s passage, DSA-LA endorsed Nithya Raman for mayor, with Raman winning 65.9% of the 1,400 votes counted . Following this, DSA NPC, passing a resolution on October 4, saying “the NPC finds DSA-LA to have violated convention resolution R22,” citing among other points the lack of clarity from Raman’s campaign on her BDS stance and DSA-LA’s unwillingness to question her about it in their candidate questionnaire. DSA-LA defended their endorsement, and Raman’s commitment to Palestinian liberation, in a letter to the NPC . While admitting their endorsement questionnaire “did not fully respond to what was laid out in R22,” DSA-LA insists that Raman has grown since 2024, writing “Raman has made progress on her positions and our chapter made the determination to endorse her as mayor. We believe her growth demonstrates the power of a DSA endorsement and our continued relational organizing.” DSA-LA cited Raman’s demand for an investigation into violence used against UCLA encampment protesters in 2024, and desire to prevent city resources from being used to aid genocide, as evidence of Raman’s evolution. Raman expressed support for ending LAPD training with Israel and rejecting any funding from organizations that profited from Palestinian occupation in her answers to DSA-LA’s questionnaire. Raman’s tenure as a city council member and mayoral candidate has made her a contentious figure in DSA circles. She was elected a member of Los Angeles City Council in 2020 with DSA-LA’s endorsement . Raman quickly gained a reputation as a progressive, making housing and tenants’ rights key aspects of her policy platform. Simultaneously, her relationship with DSA-LA soured due to her stance on Israel. Raman sought and accepted the endorsement of Democrats for Israel-Los Angeles, a pro-Israel lobbying organization . For this reason, Raman was censured by DSA-LA in 2024. “Councilmember Raman’s actions have undermined the work of DSA-LA’s Palestine Solidarity Working Group, Political Education Committee, and DSA organizers broadly,” read the statement published by DSA- LA on February 3, 2024 about the censure vote. Speaking at a mayoral debate hosted by the Jewish Federation of Los Angeles on September 29 , Raman called Israel’s actions in Gaza a genocide, but stated BDS was not part of her platform. “DSA-LA should not have endorsed Nithya Raman for the mayoral race in LA. In doing so, they have bent the rules on endorsements,” wrote Cal Poly Pomona YDSA in an emailed statement.The chapter cited New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani, and controversy around his relationship with NYPD Commissioner Jessica Titsch, as evidence for why DSA needs to be stricter with its electeds. “When we achieve state power, it should be because we have done all of the principled, necessary work required of us and that the people are willing to stand up with us, not because we compromised with the right, especially on anything to do with an active genocide happening right before our eyes.” Cal Poly Pomona YDSA also supported the NPC’s intervention: “The NPC was unequivocally right to intervene in the endorsement process, as the only way we move forward as an organization is through unified actions and standards, and to hold our chapters to account when we fail to meet those agreed-upon standards. “ The Raman campaign did not respond to requests for comment.
